programs.title: 'Allo 'Allo!
programs.desc: The first issue of the newspaper is published and the Germans are very pleased with it.On its cover there is a photo of Edith and the General.Von Klinkerhoffen invents a new propaganda trick.He decides to deepen ties with the occupied population and forces Captain Bertorelli to marry a French woman.Much to the captain's dissatisfaction, the choice falls on Madame Edith.He orders a party for the new couple at the Chateau, which will also be attended by local dignitaries.Michelle wants to use this opportunity to dispatch the English pilots who are in the Chateau's cellars, hidden in wine barrels.

programs.title: 'Allo 'Allo!
programs.desc: After escaping the Chateau, the English pilots are trapped in a canal beneath the main square of Nouvion.Monsieur Alfonse wants to open the sewer hatch, but its hinges are completely rusted.So he comes up with a brilliant plan that even Michelle would be ashamed of.René is to drive an old ice cream van right over the entrance to the canal so that he can free the pilots without any problems.Meanwhile, von Klinkerhoffen forges a portrait of the fallen Madonna.Herr Flick once again tries to win Helga's favor.Unfortunately, his beloved leaves for training and is replaced by the portly Elsa Bigstern.

programs.title: The Titan Sub Disaster: Minute by Minute
programs.desc: On June 18, 2023, the Titan submerged in the waters of the Atlantic Ocean.The five-person crew was to view the wreck of the Titanic, which lies at a depth of 3,800 meters.When the vehicle lost communication and did not surface at the right time, a race against time began.The Titan disappeared without a trace, and the whole world was engaged in the search operation.Dozens of international units: air, floating and underwater were involved in the search.Based on experts' statements, materials recorded during Titan's previous descents into the wreck area and audio recordings from the rescue operation, the program's creators analyze the course of events and ask deep-sea exploration specialists about the causes of the disaster.
